name: Condenser fan motor run capacitor
function: Phase-shifts the start/aux winding of a PSC condenser fan motor so it starts and runs in the right direction at rated torque.

availability.source: docs/manuals/lennox-1014d.pdf (Lennox LCH Series 13-25 ton Service Literature, Corp. 1014-L8, rev 05/2020) p.29
availability.note: C1, C2, C18 on all units; C19-C21 on 180-300. Not used on 180U/240U/300U.

designation.value: C1 (fan B4); C2, C18-C21 for the other fans
designation.source: docs/manuals/lennox-1014d.pdf (Lennox LCH Series 13-25 ton Service Literature, Corp. 1014-L8, rev 05/2020) p.29

location.source: docs/manuals/lennox-1014d.pdf (Lennox LCH Series 13-25 ton Service Literature, Corp. 1014-L8, rev 05/2020) p.28

lennox-lch240.sequenceRole: Fan starts when its contactor/relay closes. No cap = no start.

availability.note: Confirm the ODM is a PSC motor on this model.

failureModes.name: Lost capacitance
failureModes.goodVsBad: Measured µF outside the label tolerance.
failureModes.symptoms: Fan slow to start, runs slow and hot, may trip on internal overload.

failureModes.name: Open
failureModes.symptoms: Fan hums, won't start; spins if you nudge it (DON'T, unless locked out and verified).

failureModes.name: Shorted
failureModes.symptoms: Fan won't start; may blow fuses.

failureModes.name: Bulged / leaking case
failureModes.goodVsBad: Physical damage. Replace regardless of µF reading.

procedure: Discharge the capacitor through a resistor (not a screwdriver).
Remove at least one lead so you're only reading the capacitor.
Measure µF and compare to the label rating and tolerance (e.g. 5 µF ±6%).
Inspect the case for bulging or leaking.
safety: Caps hold charge after power is off. Discharge before touching.
Never spin a humming fan by hand on a live unit.

tolerancePct.note: Default only. Use the tolerance printed on the actual capacitor (commonly ±5, ±6 or ±10%).

marginalPct.note: Just outside label tolerance up to 10% low = marginal (replace soon); beyond = bad.

symptoms.customer: "Unit trips the breaker" or "blowing warm in the afternoon" (compressor tripping on head pressure).
symptoms.tech: Condenser fan not turning or humming, high head, HPS trips or compressor cycling on its internal overload.

confusedWith: Seized condenser fan motor bearings (also hums; spin test with power locked out)
Open condenser fan relay/contact (no voltage at the motor at all)
Dirty condenser coil (high head, but the fan is running)

labCases.context: PM visit, testing caps as a matter of course.
labCases.explanation: 9.8 µF on a 10 µF ±6% cap = 2% low, well inside tolerance.

labCases.context: Fan 1 slow to come up to speed.
labCases.explanation: 6.2 on a 10 = 38% low. Way out of tolerance. Replace.
No capacitance at all: open cap. Motor hums because it has no phase shift to start.
4.6 on a 5 is 8% low. Just outside ±6%. It'll run for now, but it's on its way out. Quote it.
